_what: Edit on canvas (src/workspace/canvas-edit-screen.tsx): any thing laid out as its parts on the canvas, each part drawn as itself, and every edit kept as one show rule (src/workspace/show-rules.json, effect `change`) whose `when` is the scope the person chose. `kinds` say what opens here (the address is /edit/<kind>:<id>): the show-rules subject its parts are decided under, the word for one part, how wide one part is drawn, and `all`, the id that lays out every one of the kind at once (titled `all_title`). A kind that already has its own canvas names it in `mounts` instead (a screen entry, src/workspace/screen-mounts.ts, and its input, `{id}` standing for the id): a site opens in the one site editor, whose canvas shows every size of a page and whose edits are the site's own draft, published from there. `subjects` say, per subject, which parts of a drawn part can be picked (`pick`, a selector inside the drawn part; `name_from`, the attribute that names one of several, such as a button's role, filled into a path's `{name}`), the fields each picked part edits (`path` inside the part's own row, `widget` a tuning-panel control, `options_from` a list under `options`), and `scopes`, each the facts of the picked part a rule must match: none is every one of its kind; several picked parts (Shift or Cmd press) are matched together. A new editable kind, part, field or scope is a row here.
